lawRefs: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-30-2.6 (rates, standard deduction, exemptions, indexing)
R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-30-12 (Social Security and pension/annuity modifications)
2026 budget (high-income surtax and Social Security changes effective tax year 2027, not 2026)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Brackets, standard deduction and exemption are the Tax Year 2026 amounts in Advisory 2025-22 (2025-11-03). One uniform rate schedule for all filing statuses. Standard deduction $11,200 single/MFS, $22,400 MFJ, $16,800 HOH; personal and dependency exemption $5,250 each. Standard deduction and exemptions phase out for modified federal AGI between $261,000 and $290,800 (phase-out increment $7,450) and are zero above that. Social Security: federally taxable benefits are fully subtracted only if the taxpayer has reached Social Security full retirement age AND federal AGI is below an indexed limit; the Tax Year 2026 limits were not yet published at retrieval (Tax Year 2025: $107,000 single/HOH/MFS, $133,750 MFJ; expect roughly 2-3% higher). Otherwise benefits are taxed as federally. Pension/401(k)/403(b)/annuity modification: up to $50,000 per person (raised from $20,000 starting Tax Year 2025) under the same full-retirement-age and AGI-limit conditions (cliff, not phased); military pensions fully exempt. From Tax Year 2027 (not in this file) the 2026 budget adds a high-income surtax (1% over $1 million in 2027, 2% in 2028, 3% from 2029) and removes the age test for the Social Security modification.
